title: quenched french salmon tart tatin
description: indulgent french dish featuring salmon, bhuna, and puff pastry, originating from normandy. a savory pastry delight suitable for dinner or lunch.
instructions: preheat the oven to 425 fahrenheit (220 c).
roll out the puff pastry to a thickness of about 1/8 inch (3 mm).
cut the puff pastry into 4 equal squares.
in a small bowl, mix together the bhuna curry paste, 1 tablespoon of unsalted butter, and 1 minced garlic clove.
spread the bhuna mixture evenly onto each puff pastry square, leaving a 1-inch (2.5 cm) border around the edges.
place a salmon fillet in the center of each pastry square.
sprinkle the grated gruyère cheese over the salmon fillet.
dot the top of each pastry square with the remaining 3 tablespoons of unsalted butter.
fold the pastry squares in half to enclose the filling and press the edges together to seal.
place the pastries on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and brush the tops with the beaten egg.
bake the pastries in the preheated oven for 18-20 minutes, or until golden brown.
while the pastries are baking, cook the sliced onion in a small saucepan over medium heat until caramelized and golden brown.
flambé the pastries with the caramelized onion and a squeeze of lemon juice for 1-2 minutes.
serve the quenched french salmon tart tatin hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley.
